card.name: Time adverbs ending a clause
card.fires_on: The last word of a time or co-occurrence adverb such as 'concomitantly', 'every' after a dose or count, 'soon' after 'very', or 'yet' after 'as of'. It fires where the phrase is complete and a new clause or phrase is expected.

modes.label: Concomitantly
modes.description: The ending of 'concomitantly' after a drug name or 'patients treated with'.
modes.example: caution should be exercised in patients treated with these agents concomit<<antly>>.

modes.label: Every after a quantity
modes.description: The word 'every' that introduces a repeat interval after a dose or count.

modes.label: Soon or yet
modes.description: A time adverb completing a phrase in general web text.
modes.example: I have an English exam very<< soon>>, so I need the answer of this

card.plain: It marks the end of a timing word like 'concomitantly' or 'every', right before the sentence moves on.
